newsitem.title: USA: TCF sees 5-10 pct cost savings in Illinois.
newsitem.headline: TCF sees 5-10 pct cost savings in Illinois.

text.p: TCF Financial Corp said Monday it expects to realize 5-10 percent in annualized cost savings from the combined operations of its Illinois bank and Standard Financial Inc once it completes the acquisition of the Chicago-based thrift.

"In the short-term, I would see somewhere between 5-10 percent cost take out in the combined Illinois operation," TCF chairmna William Cooper said in a conference call with reporters and analysts. That would be about $4 million annually, officials at the companies said.
Minneapolis-based TCF also helps to produce more than $4 million in annual revenue increases through an expanded product mix and fees for Standard Financial customers.

Meanwhile, with the planned $424 million acquisition of Standard Financial and TCF's previously announced acquisition of Winthrop Resources, TCF does not expect to make any other major acqusitions in the near future, Cooper said.

"I think it would be more likely that for a year, 18 months, you wouldn't see a good sized transaction coming down the pike with us," Cooper said. He would not rule out a deal, however, noting that acquisitions tend to be driven by opportunities.
